- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast early spikes; correct by adding 10–30% to initial forecast values.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model over-anticipates decline; correct by reducing forecast by 15–40% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp spike in true outcome (e.g., >3x prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply decay factor of 0.8–0.9 to subsequent forecast values.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; re-forecast from midpoint onward using sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day history.
- Model consistently underestimates long-term (15–30d) outcomes when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 1.2x multiplier to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast by adding 0.1–0.3 to each day’s prediction to counteract underestimation.
